title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling policies will cover legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files (Worldwide)
summary: The briefing accurately reports the revised rollout windows and the edit-and-rerun requirement for existing policies. Its licensing, prerequisites and control paths are supported; minor corrections are needed for the government-roadmap citation and a monitoring checklist step without a corresponding control row.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans service-side auto-labeling support for legacy Word .doc, Excel .xls and PowerPoint .ppt files.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview server-side auto-labeling will support legacy Microsoft Office file formats, including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt).

claims.claim: The change covers files in SharePoint.
claims.quote: Organizations can automatically evaluate and apply sensitivity labels to these files in SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Labels applying encryption to SharePoint or OneDrive content must use Assign permissions now.

claims.claim: For those encrypted labels, User access to content expires must be Never.
claims.quote: User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; rendered table
claims.claim: The Purview route is Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Mode Enable enables the specified policy for actions.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify. ... Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications. ... TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: The locations route is Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy > Choose locations where you want to apply the label.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... select the Edit policy button. ... For the page Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation <SharePointSiteLocation> adds SharePoint sites to the policy.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All ... The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites

claims.claim: The edit route is Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy.
claims.quote: Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... For a policy in the Off section, select the Edit policy button. ... For policy in the Simulation section, select the Edit policy option at the top of the page

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Comment <text> edits the optional policy comment.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify. ... The Comment parameter specifies an optional comment.

claims.claim: Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity turns on auditing when it is off.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. ... Select the Audit solution card. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true enables auditing in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell. ... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true ... You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Items to review shows the files matching the simulation rules.
claims.quote: For policies in simulation mode, select the Items to review tab to see which emails or documents matched the rules that you specified.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: TestWithoutNotifications keeps an auto-labeling policy in test mode.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter adds OneDrive locations to a policy.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: Whether a PowerShell policy edit restarts the crawl for legacy files is not specifically documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview legacy Office auto-labeling Comment crawl; opened Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy and apply-sensitivity-label-automatically and read MC1530948. The reference documents comment edits, not their legacy-crawl effect; the notice gives no PowerShell-specific explanation.

claims.claim: Existing auto-labeling policy controls govern the legacy-format change rather than a separate legacy-specific switch.
claims.quote: Admins manage the capability through Microsoft Purview auto-labeling policies. Microsoft Learn identifies the Microsoft Purview portal's Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies surface for service-side auto-labeling.

claims.claim: The notice's labeling impact concerns legacy files within the SharePoint and OneDrive locations covered by a policy, not locations outside it.
claims.quote: The change expands the files that auto-labeling policies can evaluate and label to include legacy .doc, .xls, and .ppt files in SharePoint and OneDrive, according to the request.
